title: Runtime kernel apprentice: seq-len buckets and latency calibrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Improve per-request kernel choice accuracy while bounding latency SLO regressions by using a lightweight "apprentice" that combines offline microbench profiles with an online latency calibrator.

Context:
- We have many microkernels with different cost/latency characteristics across hardware (H100/A100/T4) and sequence lengths. Current static heuristics overindex on average-case throughput and occasionally pick kernels that regress p95 on tail-heavy workloads.
- Prior work produced large profiling corpora (see dependencies) but we lack a compact runtime policy that adapts quickly when workload shift occurs (e.g., chat with long context vs short queries).

Proposal:
1) Offline phase: build compact performance fingerprints for a small set of canonical seq-len buckets (0-16, 17-64, 65-256, 257-1024). For each bucket we record: avg latency, p95, TPU/GPU occupancy proxy, memory hotness, and a few scalar features to estimate decode vs prefill tradeoffs. Fingerprints are stored as small vectors indexed by (arch, model-family, quantization-profile).
2) Runtime "apprentice": a low-cost policy that selects the top-2 candidate kernels from fingerprint lookup and then runs a 1-2 microprobe decode on a short prefill prefix (when safe) to capture live latency divergence. The apprentice uses an exponential moving average (EMA) calibrator to align offline predictions with live tail behavior.
3) Safety & fallback: if the calibrator observes sustained p95 drift over threshold or microprobe fails (OOM or kernel error), automatically degrade to conservative kernel with known latency safety (slightly higher cost but stable).
4) Rollout plan: test in a canary cohort (5% traffic) with A/B measurement for p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU util, and cost/TU. If tail improves >5% w/o cost >3% regression, expand to 25% then 100%.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Microprobes add small extra work; limit to requests predicted to be borderline (within margin of error) to avoid overhead on all requests.
- Some models/pinned quantizations may not support microprobing; fall back to pure fingerprint choice.
- Must ensure microprobe does not leak user data from private deployments; microprobe only uses request prefix cache local to request and respects KMS/HSM constraints.

Success metrics:
- p95 latency reduction or no regressions (target: p95 <= baseline + 2% for 95% of tenants)
- p50 improvement or stable
- tokens/sec change within +/-3% overall
- rollback rate zero in canary (no critical errors)

Deliverables:
- Microbenchmark harness and fingerprint generator (offline job)
- Apprentice runtime library + safe fallback hooks
- Telemetry: per-request kernel choice, microprobe outcome, calibrator state, drift alerts
- Canary rollout dashboard and automated rollback action

Open questions:
- Best bucket boundaries for mixed workloads (currently proposing 4 buckets)
- How long to warm EMA calibrator per model/tenant (start 1 minute, tune)
- Whether to permit microprobe on cold-start requests in Dedicated/Private where prefill cost sensitivity is higher

comments: 2026-02-22 - Liam Chen: Spun up the offline fingerprint job on a1.large; initial CSVs look sane. Found a big divergence on H100 decode kernels at seq 320 where p95 spikes 40% relative to offline profile.

2026-02-25 - Marisol Vega (review): Design looks good. Please add a section on telemetry retention and privacy for Private customers. Also specify the exact thresholds for drift alerts — we need conservative defaults for HA tenants.

2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Updated design to include privacy constraints: microprobe limited to first 64 tokens of request and sanitized logs. Added default drift thresholds: p95 delta > 8% sustained over 3 minutes triggers fallback.

2026-03-04 - Ethan Brooks (eng review): Prototype microprobe implementation exists in branch feature/kernel-apprentice. Observations: 1) microprobe overhead is ~0.6ms on average on A100 for 8-token prefix; 2) occasional kernel compile on H100 adds 15-30ms — added compile-bypass in runtime for canary to avoid false positives.

2026-03-08 - Liam Chen: Canary ready — configured 5% traffic on runtime-canary cluster (region us-west2). Dashboards: runtime/kernel-apprentice-canary (Grafana). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2041

2026-03-10 - QA (Sumi Park): Smoke tests passed for basic throughput/latency. Observed one private deployment that disabled microprobes due to policy — noted in telemetry. Proceeding with metrics collection for 72h before expanding rollout.
